content:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert created: INCIDENT AS-4351 for customer AstraMed — prod EU — high 5xx rate on private VPC ingress. Thread started by incidents-bot.

incidents-bot: Page sent to @sara_oncall (primary on-call). Please acknowledge.

sara_oncall: ack — I'm looking. Can someone paste a quick symptom summary? 503s only or also increased latency?

alex_support: customer reports 503 and failed webhook deliveries since ~09:12 UTC. All requests hitting their private tenant show 503s. No recent code change on their side.

mike_neteng: quick note: we migrated AstraMed's ingress from ALB -> NLB yesterday to preserve client IPs for their mTLS setup. NLBs are L4 so backend now expects SNI/Host bits to be present differently. Suspect healthchecks/Host header mismatch.

jia_sre: Can you share recent target health? run:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-astramed-prod/abcdef123456
```
and paste output.

mike_neteng: pasted output snippet:
```
TargetHealthDescriptions:
  - Id: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f
    HealthStatus: unhealthy
    Reason: HTTP_5XX
    Description: "Response missing Host header / invalid http response"
  - Id: i-0b2c3d4e5f6g
    HealthStatus: healthy
    Reason: 
```

alex_support: customer-side logs show long TTFB and then 503. No client cert errors — looks like backend returned 503 from app after failing virtual host lookup.

ada_devops: fwiw, NLB -> target group healthcheck performs TCP/HTTP differently. We probably left the healthcheck set to HTTP with Host header "astra.example.com" which ALB supplied before. NLB healthcheck probes may not include Host header unless configured with proper SNI/proxy protocol.

pm_elena: customer SLA: <5m downtime acceptable. They need a fast, transparent mitigation. Can we do an in-place fix that doesn't require app deploy?

sara_oncall: triage plan: 1) try switching target-group healthcheck to TCP:443 so ELB only validates socket up — quick flip, low risk. 2) if healthy, gradually shift Route53 weights back to EU pool. 3) longer term: reconfigure NLB with Proxy Protocol v2 or add a tiny sidecar to respond to Host header healthcheck. I'll take action 1 now.

jia_sre: +1. If TCP healthcheck returns green, we can re-register unhealthy targets. Doing the modify now.

jia_sre: command run:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-astramed-prod/abcdef123456 \
  --health-check-protocol TCP --health-check-port 443
```

mike_neteng: also adding temporary SG rule to allow ELB healthcheck origin CIDR (we allowed ALB range before). Add ingress from 10.200.12.0/24 tcp:443 for the node group.

mike_neteng: SG update command (applied):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.200.12.0/24
```

alex_support: notifying customer that we're performing quick network-level mitigations and healthcheck change.

incidents-bot: Health-check change detected: target-group tg-astramed-prod now using TCP:443. Re-evaluating target health.

jia_sre: new describe-target-health shows 5/5 healthy within ~40s. Unhealthy targets started passing.

mike_neteng: routing: we kept Route53 weights steady, but backend pool is now healthy. I'm seeing 503s drop to baseline in metrics.

alex_support: customer confirms API responses recovered at 09:28 UTC. They reported transient failures ~16 minutes.

pm_elena: customer wants root cause and rollback plan. What broke exactly?

ada_devops: root cause summary: ALB->NLB migration removed HTTP host/header rewriting semantics that ALB previously provided; backend app relied on Host header for virtual host resolution and healthcheck endpoint. NLB healthchecks were hitting the backend without Host header causing app to return 5xx; target group marked unhealthy which caused connection churn and 503s. Additionally SG only allowed ALB healthcheck CIDRs, not the NLB node IPs, amplifying the issue.

sara_oncall: short-term mitigation implemented: TCP healthcheck + temporary SG ingress from 10.200.12.0/24. Both are lower-risk and restored traffic.

sara_oncall: medium-term actions (ticketed):
- Add Proxy Protocol v2 / SNI support on NLB and ensure backend can parse it, or insert a tiny proxy that injects Host header.
- Update infra docs and runbook for ALB->NLB migrations (check Host header, healthcheck semantics, SG source ranges).
- Add automated post-migration smoke that verifies host-based responses (HTTP 200 for /health with Host header).

pm_elena: please create customer-facing RCA and include timeline. I will coordinate a follow-up call.

jia_sre: taking ownership for follow-ups. Handoff: I'll remain the incident lead for next 6 hours. @sara_oncall handing off.

sara_oncall: Handoff ack — back to standby. Good job team. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident AS-4351 marked RESOLVED (mitigated) at 09:36 UTC by jia_sre.

alex_support: closing internal thread once RCA draft is in Google Drive.

pm_elena: customer update message sent. They appreciate quick mitigation but requested a postmortem with timeline and permanent fix ETA.

jia_sre: will open RFC for NLB proxy/protocol changes and link in the RCA ticket.

sara_oncall: leaving a short runbook note: if future NLB migrations, first check healthcheck protocol and SG for node CIDRs, then toggle healthcheck to TCP if app can't accept Host-less probes.

mike_neteng: tagging infra to add a validation in the infra PR template.

ada_devops: :white_check_mark: — done.

end of thread.
